abstract: We study coloring extensions over an induced chromatic vertex-critical core. Our new contact-bound theorems remove prescribed core-order, deficit and exterior-arboricity bounds. For every $k\ge3$, a $K_k$-free graph is $k$-colorable when its exterior consists of a nonempty connected set of vertices of total degree at most $k$ and one hub with at most $k-1$ core neighbors. For nine colors, we also treat two hubs over a connected $K_7$-free low-degree remainder: the whole-graph Euler inequality suffices if each hub has at most seven core neighbors, or at most eight when the hubs are nonadjacent. The proofs are by hand. Connectivity propagates minimal list obstructions across the exterior, and adaptive core recoloring forces common leaf neighborhoods. In the two-hub case, failed extension forces their core neighborhoods to cover the core, deriving an order bound rather than assuming one; Gallai's edge bound and Euler then contradict failure. The geometric exclusion of all-low seven-cliques gives necessary hub-contact alternatives in a globally minimum biplanar counterexample. We retain the earlier sparse-exterior theorems at core deficit eight or nine, and the arbitrary-core-order arboricity-three theorem at deficit five, with their evidence unchanged. Small standard-library checks corroborate the new list identities and a classical disconnected hypothesis control. These results choose a core coloring; they do not guarantee that an arbitrary counterexample has the required connected remainder, hub count or contact bounds. The Earth–Moon problem remains open.

change_summary: Adds Theorems6/7 and Corollary8, with complete hand proofs in Section13. One hub: arbitrary k, no density/order bounds, connected low remainder and <=k-1 core contacts. Two hubs: K9-free+Euler, connected K7-free low remainder, <=7 contacts each or <=8 for nonadjacent hubs. Failure derives core coverage and q<=12/14; Gallai/Euler finish. Imports Paper23v4 all-low-K7 reduction only for GLOBAL minimum biplanar corollary. Retains earlier results and every prior supplement file byte for byte. Adds optional finite list-identity audits and classical disconnected controls. Generalized title/abstract; attribution to earlier joint mechanisms retained. No core-occurrence or global Earth–Moon claim.

coauthors.contribution: Retained-core density and recoloring framework; original generalization and joint proof audit; three-forest deficit-five theorem, one-high reduction, two-high leaf and component-savings arguments, Gallai flexibility and final closure; joint revision preparation.
